topic: Gateway Bulkheads Halt Ingress Thread Starvation
postText:
When a secondary lab integration stalled during a busy hospital shift, our entire API Gateway stopped accepting incoming traffic.

Triage, billing, and pharmacy calls froze instantly—not because those services failed, but because edge worker threads starved waiting on one slow backend socket.

In mission-critical healthcare IT, edge resilience determines overall survival. Without strict boundary isolation, slow downstream responses saturate gateway connection pools. A single degraded microservice triggers cascading thread starvation across edge proxies, turning a localized bottleneck into complete system downtime.

We solved this cascading failure with three coordinated edge patterns:

1. Ingress Bulkhead Partitioning: Allocate dedicated concurrency limits per downstream route. If the lab integration hangs, it depletes only its assigned 20 worker threads, leaving remaining gateway pools free to serve emergency and inpatient traffic.

2. Token Bucket Rate Limiting: Apply edge rate limiting to shed excess spikes before requests acquire downstream execution handles, shielding internal topologies.

3. Dynamic Circuit Breaking: When downstream latency exceeds 500ms across a 10-second rolling window, trip the breaker instantly. Return fast 503s or cached fallbacks immediately instead of tying up gateway sockets.

How do you configure gateway bulkheads and timeouts to keep one degraded service from dragging down edge proxies?
